chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whoever prays the Maghrib prayer and then prays four rak'at after it, and does not speak until he has prayed ten rak'at, reading in each rak'at Al-Hamd and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad', it is equivalent to freeing ten slaves."

key_terms.عِدْلَ: Equivalent to / Equal in value to

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying four rak'at after Maghrib without speaking?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Rida’s (AS) teaching on the virtue of *Salat al-Mudtir*, where praying four rak'at after Maghrib without speech yields the reward of freeing ten slaves. This practice emphasizes the spiritual discipline of *samt* (silence) to preserve the sanctity of the prayer sequence, reflecting the Shia emphasis on continuous devotion (*mudawamah*) and the tangible merit of specific supererogatory acts.
